findings.title: Skip-restart attribution gap continued from W1 (now spanning W0+W1+W2)
findings.detail: Per F-0.2.18-W1-001 precedent. settings.json env was updated to AHO_WORKSTREAM=W2 last night but session never restarted, so claude-code's OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES still carry aho.workstream=W0 (the boot-time value from W0 — never even re-flowed to W1 because that restart also didn't happen). Aho-emitted structured events (workstream_start/complete, audit, acceptance archives) correctly tag W2 as event content. Cost-attribution per Pillar 8 lands all W0+W1+W2 spend on W0 in this session. Recoverable post-hoc via timestamp reconciliation; materiality (ADR-0010) unaffected (counts archives by content, not span tags). Pattern is now extensively documented; carry-forward to ADR formalizing 'session-restart vs in-session-deviation' contract for future iterations.

findings.title: bin/aho-models is Tier-1-only; ollama upstream install.sh currently broken
findings.detail: bin/aho-models hard-requires nvidia-smi + 8GB VRAM minimum; model-fleet.txt is the Tier-1 set (qwen3.5:9b, GLM-4.6V-Flash-9B, llama3.2:3b, nemotron-mini). No base-tier code path. Compounded: pacman-packages.txt comment directs to upstream ollama install via curl|sh, but that script's .tgz fallback URL returns 404 because GitHub releases now ship .tar.zst only (Ollama v0.24.0). Manual workaround this session: install-base-tier-models.fish uses pacman ollama 0.23.2-1.1 (one minor behind upstream but stable) and pulls llama3.2:3b + nomic-embed-text directly. Marks install.state step 4 pass.
findings.0.3.1_scope: Tier-aware bin/aho-models (tier-detect + branch behavior); per-tier model fleet files; aho-models install method = pacman by default (re-evaluate vs upstream once install.sh is fixed); _check_vram handles nvidia-smi-binary-present-driver-broken case via exit-status check not stdout-parse.

findings.title: install.fish has no tier.json writer; plan-doc §W2 expects it but no aho subcommand creates it
findings.detail: Plan-doc §W2 explicitly says install.fish writes ~/.config/aho/tier.json with host_id/tier/deployment_mode/families/bundle. grep of src/aho/ + bin/ found no writer for that path. tier-detect.py writes a marker file at /var/run/aho/tier (different path, different shape — just the tier label). Manual workaround this session: provision-w2-acceptance.fish writes the file with correct shape.
findings.0.3.1_scope: Add `aho install tier-manifest` subcommand (or fold into install.fish step 7 systemd as a pre-service step) that calls tier-detect, gathers per-host metadata, writes ~/.config/aho/tier.json. Update plan-doc references to match actual writer name.

findings.title: No aho-secrets-broker.service template in templates/systemd/; ADR-0009 broker-per-host not realized by install.fish
findings.detail: templates/systemd/ holds 7 templates (openclaw, nemoclaw, telegram, harness-watcher, jaeger, otel-collector, dashboard) but no aho-secrets-broker.service. bin/aho-systemd installs 4 (openclaw, nemoclaw, telegram, harness-watcher) — broker not in that set. ADR-0009 says every host runs its own broker — implementation gap. Manual workaround this session: provision-w2-acceptance.fish writes the unit on a8 and starts it.
findings.0.3.1_scope: Add templates/systemd/aho-secrets-broker.service.template to repo. Add 'secrets-broker' to bin/aho-systemd $daemons list. Verify unit installs cleanly on NZXTcos + a8 + future hosts.

findings.title: Plan-doc broker socket path (~/.local/share/aho/broker/broker.sock) differs from aho code default ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/aho-secrets.sock)
findings.detail: Plan-doc §W2 #3 says broker socket exists at ~/.local/share/aho/broker/broker.sock. Code (src/aho/host/secrets_broker.py default_socket_path) returns $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/aho-secrets.sock — typically /run/user/UID/aho-secrets.sock. XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is on tmpfs with mode 0700 perms — better engineering than persistent-fs storage for runtime sockets. This W2 acceptance used the code default; plan-doc path treated as aspirational.
findings.0.3.1_scope: ADR-0009 amendment to document canonical broker socket path = $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/aho-secrets.sock. Update plan-doc templates accordingly.

findings.title: Substrate-operational learnings during W2 (pre-install + post-install sidequests)
findings.detail: Multiple operational discoveries during W2 substrate work, none harness-relevant but worth recording: (a) Kyle's sudo locked out via PAM faillock default deny=3 from samba-setup attempts — recovered via reboot (faillock state in /run tmpfs) and biometrics login; provisioned `break_glass` wheel-group user as future insurance (recorded in feedback-break-glass-account-a8 memory). (b) Dolphin file-mount sidequest: SMB install on a8 (samba 4.24.2) reached running state but smbd loopback-only due to samba's `bind interfaces only` + tun device flakiness; Kyle pivoted to fish:// (KDE's SSH-based KIO) which Just Worked — samba removed from both hosts. (c) Enabled real sshd on a8 + added LAN-direct ufw rules + /etc/hosts overrides for jumbo-capable LAN bypass of Tailscale 1280-MTU tunnel; NZXTcos NIC reconfigured to MTU 9000 with persistent NM setting. (d) bin/aho-python had a fish-command-cache bug masking newly-installed CLI as 'not on PATH' — patched in repo (test -x replaces command -q).

findings.title: bin/aho-python used fish's cached `command -q` to check CLI presence — patched in-session
findings.detail: bin/aho-python step's post-install check was `command -q aho` (fish builtin). The check returned stale-negative because fish's command lookup cache was populated before pip installed aho into ~/.local/bin/. Patched to `test -x $HOME/.local/bin/aho` (file existence check, cache-immune). The doctor path (_cmd_doctor) at bin/aho-python:48 has the same pattern but is only hit in a fresh-shell context where the cache is clean — left alone but worth sweeping in 0.3.1.

findings.title: pacman-packages.txt was missing podman; added in-session
findings.detail: a8 was rebuilt between W0 probe and W2, losing podman. install.fish's bin/aho-pacman doesn't install podman because pacman-packages.txt didn't declare it. Added `podman` to the list with a 0.2.18-W2 comment. Carry-forward applies to future deployments — they pick up podman automatically on first install.fish run.

Not a real finding — the small model treated its own prompt as if it were an artifact entry.
